second.QA1_evidence: Model, gradients, data generator and optimizer are all specified: Hamiltonian Eq. (16), exact gradient Eq. (18), bound gradient Eqs. (30)-(33), data from Eq. (57), BFGS with exact diagonalization. Quote: "In all our examples, we choose p = 0.9 and M = 8." (Section IV). Gaps: initial values of b and w, the random mode centers and BFGS settings are not stated.
second.QA2_evidence: Classical numerical execution is stated and qubit counts are given, but no circuit depth or layer count is reported (the model is a thermal state of a transverse-field Ising Hamiltonian, not a circuit) and no shots (expectations are exact). Quotes: "This can be done using exact diagonalization for small systems." and "a fully connected model with N = 10 qubits" (Section IV.A). Hardware is only discussed as a prospect (Section V).
second.QA3_evidence: A classical Boltzmann machine with the same units and connectivity is trained on the same data with the same optimizer (BFGS) and scored with the same KL divergence; the QBM adds one shared parameter Gamma. Quote: "Classical BM will have N + N(N-1)/2 = N(N+1)/2 trainable parameters" (Section IV.A; Figs. 2a, 3a, 4).
second.QA4_evidence: Small synthetic data that is reproducible from a stated formula, not a public benchmark; metric is KL divergence, Eq. (58). Quote: "the training data was generated as a mixture of M factorized distributions" (Section IV, Eq. 57).
second.QA5_evidence: No repository, code or data link anywhere in the paper; the only URL printed is a Wikipedia page for BFGS (reference [25]). No availability statement.
second.execution: Classical simulation by exact diagonalization of the quantum model (transverse-field Ising Boltzmann distribution; not a gate circuit). No quantum hardware run; use of a quantum annealer is discussed only as a possibility (Section V).
second.scale: Qubits: N = 10 (fully visible, Section IV.A); 8 visible + 2 hidden = 10 (restricted QBM, Section IV.B); N = 11 as 8 inputs + 3 outputs (Section IV.C). Circuit depth or layer count: not stated (not a circuit model). Shots: not stated (expectations computed exactly).
second.classical_baseline: Classical Boltzmann machine with the same number of units and the same connectivity, N(N+1)/2 parameters, trained with BFGS on the same Bernoulli-mixture data and compared by KL divergence (Figs. 2 to 4). Also bQBM-CE, a bound-based QBM using the classical positive-phase expression (Section IV.B).
